differences.what: massing: the draft's generic hipped block is now the photograph's house: a stone front of two storeys and a short attic storey over a raised basement under a very steep slated roof with iron cresting, the cornice's top near 13.25 m; the front receding left to the south, the north flank at the right

the round tower on the sheet's bay, three stages of bent sashes to a slated cone with a finial; the north corner block with the door at the stoop's head and its chamber and attic windows over it; the south gable with its arched pair, chamber pair and attic light
the high stoop of eleven risers between solid stone cheek walls ending in block newels, and the low iron railing on its coping along the walk
the tall stone stack off the north flank behind the corner block
the tower's third stage: built 1.0 m over the main cornice (K01's least clearance for a tower), where the photograph springs the cone at the cornice's level, so the cone stands about 1 m high

the corbelled corner turret on the north flank behind the corner block's front corner (x 1050-1145, y 520-760 px): built (T-3290) a round 1.4 m across on the wall's plane at s 2.8 from the front corner, its two silhouettes within 6 px of the photograph's, standing on the attic belt, one light turned toward the avenue, a moulded cornice and a steep slated cone leaning on the mansard and toward the stack

the corner turret stands about 0.55 m low: its wall top 12.25 m where the photograph's cornice runs level with the main cornice (about 12.8 m to its bed), so its cornice draws about 45 px under the photograph's and its light is 1.25 m tall against about 1.45 m; K01 holds an oriel's wall top a metre under the main eave unless the eave dies into it, which the kit does only on a street front under a hip or gable

the corner turret's foot: built a turned stone foot (a 0.3 m round, from 10.25 m to the attic floor) where the photograph's attic belt sweeps round the turret (y 745-800 px); the 1883 plate draws a corbel with a pendant (album_1883), under the bar either way
the north flank's front window column under the turret (x 1060-1120 px): first built at s 1.7, 1.1 m nearer the corner than the photograph's camera puts it; now at s 2.8, under the turret's axis

the dormers' ornament: the photograph's are stone wall dormers with crocketed gables, pinnacles and finials; now built faced in the front's stone, a stone coping up each rake with crockets on its back (two a rake on the north dormer, three on the south), a square pinnacle engaged at each edge of the face from the cornice past the gable's foot under a cap and a pyramid, and a turned finial at the apex (T-3293)

the south dormer's height: the photograph's rises from the cornice nearly to the cone's shoulder (x 270-400, y 120-500 px), its finial a cross-like knop; built on the record's 1.5 m sash under a 60 degree gable, so it stands lower and most of it falls behind the tower from this camera (T-3294)

the south gable: its copings now carry three crockets a rake between the kneelers' pinnacles and the apex finial (T-3293); the arched pair is two round-headed lights either side of a mullion (T-3292), where the photograph draws them under one enclosing arch with a hood, which is not built (T-3294)

the entrance: the door now stands in a deep round-arched recess under a moulded voussoir ring with a keystone, a radial fanlight over a pair of leaves (T-3292), its crown just over the tower's principal lights' heads as the photograph's shows over the awning (x 760-830, y 1200-1225 px)
the ivy over the south part of the front and the tower, to the attic floor
the stone's tone: built the register's brownstone; the monochrome print reads lighter, which a print cannot settle

the camera: its solve lands on its bounds (29.6 px RMS, 99 px at the gable's apex), so the render draws the house smaller and flatter than the photograph's close, steep view; the gaps that follow from the camera alone are within tolerance
the south flank and the rear, and the sheet's stone wing on the south flank's rear half (T-3278)

the tower stands 0.17 m further out and the south gable 0.05 m more proud than first built, so the kit closes the gable's window recesses and holds the tower's finial clear of the wall's plane (T-3277's lap); under the 0.3 m bar

the tower's finial: now built turned (T-3293), the kit's knobs on a waisted shaft 2.4 m over the cone's apex as the photograph's is (x 420-450, y 0-110 px), with no collar on the cone, so its widest knob (0.15 m from the axis) stands clear of the wall's plane the axis is 0.17 m in front of and nothing of it is clipped
the entrance's carved capitals on the pilasters either side of the arch (x 680-710 and 880-915, y 1195-1225 px) are not built (T-3294)
the striped canvas awning over the door: a seasonal fitting of undated state, kept off the 1904 build as T-1900's phase guard asks (separate the undated awning from the geometry)

the south pair's lights draw narrower than the photograph's (about 60 px against 105 px at this scale, where the tower's lights draw 35 against 50): the camera's fit is weakest at that end (54 px at the pair's sill), so the two disagree by less than its error

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
